text: Gallant means brave and noble, and polite too. Here, a prefect in a Harry Potter film is a hero with good manners.
Beguiling means so charming that it pulls you in, almost like a spell. Here, the wartime years are called beguiling because the spies were such colorful people.
An eccentric is someone with odd habits that are harmless and interesting, like a neighbor who walks a goose on a leash. Here, the spies of wartime Britain were full of them.
To cast an actor means to choose them for a part in a movie. Here, a new James Bond has been chosen.
A role is a part an actor plays in a movie or show. Here, the role is James Bond.
A spy is a person who secretly gathers information about other countries or groups. Bond is a made-up spy.
Undistinguished means ordinary, not famous or special. Here, Ian Fleming is described as a not very famous journalist before he wrote Bond.
An enthusiast is someone who loves a hobby very much. Here, Fleming was a bird-watching enthusiast.
Comely is an old-fashioned word for good-looking. Fleming wanted pretty heroines in his book.
Vast means extremely large. Here, Fleming hoped to earn a huge amount of money.
Dull means boring, with nothing exciting about it. Dull, duller, dullest are the three steps of comparing. Here, Fleming found the bird book and its author's name very boring.
A grebe is a small swimming bird that lives near lakes and ponds. Here, the bird book had pages about one kind.
Unromantic means plain, with no dreamy or fancy feeling. Here, the name Bond sounds short and plain.
Masculine means having qualities traditionally linked with men, like strength. Here, the name sounded tough and manly to Fleming.
Anglo-Saxon here means plain and English-sounding, from the old peoples who lived in England long ago. Fleming meant the name Bond sounded simple and very English.
A franchise is a group of books, films or games that share the same hero or world and keep being made. Here, Bond is a huge one.
Purists are people who want something kept exactly the way it always was. Here, some Bond fans are worried about the change.
A martini is a kind of mixed drink for adults. Bond is famous for ordering one in the movies.
Sultry here means mysterious and moody in an attractive way. It can also describe hot, sticky weather.
Box office means ticket sales for movies. Someone who is a box-office draw is an actor whose name brings in lots of ticket buyers.
A draw here is a person or thing that attracts a crowd. It is not about pictures with a pencil.
To suck the life out of something means to drain away what makes it fun or special. Here, it is a joke about the vampire role, as fans fear the actor will ruin Bond.
A prefect is an older student chosen to help keep order at some British schools. Here, it is a character in Harry Potter.
An adaptation is a book, play or story changed into a movie or show. Here, the Odyssey film is one.
Subtle means gentle and not obvious. A subtle actor shows feelings in small ways, not big ones.
A lunk is a slow, clumsy person who is not very clever. Here, the writer jokes that Bond is a bit of one.
A cardboard booby is Fleming's joke for a flat, dull person with no depth, like a cutout made of cardboard.
To gross money means to earn it in total, before subtracting costs. Here, the films earned over $23 billion.
Inflation is when prices slowly rise over time, so a dollar buys less. Adjusting for it lets you compare old money fairly with new money.
Psychologically means to do with the mind and feelings. Here, Bond matters to how Britain feels about itself.
A has-been is someone or something that used to be important but is not anymore. Here, Britain feels like one among world powers.
Succour is help and comfort when times are hard. Here, Bond comforts Britain by being a hero.
Puny means small and weak. Here, the writer says Britain's army is small compared with the past.
Shaky means not steady or strong. Here, Britain's economy is not doing well.
A baddy is the bad guy, the villain, in a story.
National import means something important to a whole country. Here, choosing Bond is treated like big news for Britain.
Britannia is the old name for Britain, shown in art as a woman with a shield and helmet. She stands for the country itself.
Loaded here means carrying extra feelings or hidden meaning. A loaded choice makes people argue.
Creative control means the power to decide how a movie or show is made. Here, an American studio now has it.
To betray means to be disloyal to someone or something. Here, a good adaptation should stay true to both eras of a story.
Smoulder means to burn slowly. Here, it is a way of saying a romantic, intense look.
Derring-do is old-fashioned for daring, brave action. Here, wartime spies were full of it.
A commando is a soldier trained for quick, dangerous missions. Fleming met many in the wartime navy.
Naval intelligence is the part of the navy that collects secret information. Fleming worked there in wartime.
To surrender is to give up in a fight or war. Here, an officer accepted a city's surrender.
MI6 is Britain's agency that gathers secret information abroad. James Bond is said to work for it.
An intelligence service is a government group that gathers secret information about other countries.
A spymaster is the person in charge of spies.
A precursor is something that came before and led to something later. Here, one bureau was the earlier version of MI6.
Notorious means famous for something bad.
Perfunctory means done quickly without much care or interest.
Mystique is a special, mysterious feeling that makes something seem exciting.
Adolescent means to do with the teenage years, and it can also mean childish. Here, Fleming joked about his own books.
Workmanlike means done in a plain, competent way, without anything fancy.
A repetition is something said or done again. Here, Fleming used the same words often in his books.
To savour is to enjoy something slowly and fully.
A villain is the bad character in a story.
A misogynist is someone who dislikes or looks down on women. Here, a character calls old Bond one.
Here dinosaur is a joke for a person or idea that is badly out of date.
Reinvention means changing something so much it feels new again.
Mores are the habits and rules a society believes in. Modern mores means what people today think is right.
Traditionalists are people who want to keep old ways. Here, they are the fans who dislike changes to Bond.
If your hands are tied, you cannot act freely. Here, the writers face a hard problem, just like Bond tied to a chair.
